method: Headless Chromium 1280x900 dsf1, 3s settle, then 5s windows at top, middle, bottom, a 5s mouse-circle stress (16ms) at top, and a hidden-tab test (visibilityState and hidden overridden plus visibilitychange), measuring rAF fps, CDP TaskDuration and ScriptDuration as % of window, and longtask count; every team run twice and averaged (script: judges/performance/perf.js, raw: raw.jsonl). Run 1 was noisier for all teams, so the ranking leans on both runs together.

matter.best: Hidden test passes: busy drops to 1.1% avg (0.7 and 1.5) and the page pauses. Lowest heap among the four (2.1MB).
matter.worst: Highest main-thread load and the most canvas area: 21 canvases, 4.42M px total. Avg busy 75.8% of the window, 33.8% script, about 48 longtasks per run across the 4 active windows, and the mouse stress was the worst case (85.5% and 83.8% busy, 16 to 38 fps).
matter.evidence: Avg across 2 runs and 4 active windows: 35.6 fps, 75.8% task, 33.8% script, 48 longtasks. Run1 top 19.7fps/88.4%/24 LT, mid 33.6/70.5/13, bottom 20.4/81.1/19, mouse 16.2/85.5/29. Run2 top 51.8/72.7/0, mid 59.0/48.7/0, bottom 45.5/75.5/5, mouse 38.5/83.8/6. Even the good run never held 60fps at the top or under mouse stress. Heap 2.0 to 2.1MB, canvasPx 4423879. Hidden: 0.7% and 1.5% busy.

signal.best: Idle middle section is cheap (39.8% and 21.7% busy, 38.9 to 60 fps), so offscreen canvases are being gated. Hidden test passes: 0.7% and 1.1% busy.
signal.worst: Top of page and mouse stress are heavy: 74% to 86% busy with script near 42% to 48%, and 12 longtasks in the run 1 mouse test. Run 1 bottom had 20 longtasks.
signal.evidence: Avg: 46.4 fps, 63.1% task, 34.1% script, 28.5 longtasks per run. Run1 top 35.8fps/80.8%/15 LT, mid 38.9/39.8/8, bottom 32.1/76.1/20, mouse 37.6/86.4/12. Run2 top 51.6/76.6/2, mid 60/21.7/0, bottom 60.1/49.2/0, mouse 54.9/73.9/0. 20 canvases, 3.73M px, heap 1.7 to 3.1MB. Hidden 0.7% and 1.1% busy.

sky.best: Fewest canvases (6, 4.11M px) and good smoothness on mouse stress (43.9 and 57.2 fps). Hidden test passes (1.2% and 0.7% busy, and it is the only page that listens for visibilitychange).
sky.worst: The footer is the heaviest spot measured for any team: run 1 bottom was 95.3% busy at 17.2 fps with 48 longtasks, and run 2 bottom was 72.7% with 44.3 fps. Middle is also never cheap (79.0% and 61.8% busy), so it keeps working at full cost wherever you are.

creatures.best: Clearly the most efficient: near 60fps in every window in run 2 (59.9, 60, 60, 59.9) with zero longtasks, and only 4 longtasks per run on average. Busy time is the lowest everywhere (32.9% to 48.3% in run 2). The mouse stress costs almost nothing extra (48.3% busy at 59.9 fps).
creatures.worst: Still uses 19 canvases and carries the highest heap (3.5 to 3.7MB, vs 1.7 to 3.1MB for others). Busy time is still 33% to 60% in a headless software renderer, so nothing is truly idle. Run 1 top had 6 longtasks during the load settle.
creatures.evidence: Avg: 57.2 fps, 46.6% task, 27.2% script, 4.0 longtasks per run. Run1 top 50.3/59.5/6, mid 50.6/51.5/2, bottom 57.7/43.5/0, mouse 59.4/52.2/0. Run2 top 59.9/46.5/0, mid 60/32.9/0, bottom 60/38.6/0, mouse 59.9/48.3/0. canvasPx 3367770 (smallest total area of the four). Hidden 0.7% and 0.8% busy.

one_line_verdict: Creatures held about 57 fps with roughly 47% busy time and almost no long tasks, while the other three sat at 63% to 76% busy with 28 to 48 long tasks per run, so it wins by a wide margin.
